_comment: Drift guard for the vendored accepted-risk gate. `sha256` is of the file AS VENDORED (header included); `canonical_sha256` is of the upstream GIT BLOB at `canonical_commit` - LF bytes, reproducible from a clone of canonical_repo with `git show <canonical_commit>:<canonical_path> | sha256sum`. Use the COMMIT: `canonical_version` is an iterate run id, not a git ref, so it cannot be resolved - which is why this field was added. The hash is NOT a working-tree hash either: on Windows core.autocrlf=true yields a CRLF variant matching no upstream blob, which is what every canonical_sha256 held until iterate-2026-07-31-revendor-accepted-risk-gate. Only `sha256` is enforced automatically (tests/test_accepted_risks_vendored.py, both directions: every entry resolves to a file whose hash matches, and every vendored module has an entry); `canonical_sha256` is provenance for the next re-vendor, verified by hand against a clone, by recorded decision - the offline check would need a sibling clone that is not guaranteed present.
